Rashi on Niddah 31b:10:1.english: She regrets [her oath] after seven [days] - And she desires intercourse with her husband so that she may again conceive a male.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:11:1.english: For what [reason is] circumcision on the eighth [day] - And not on the seventh [day].

Rashi on Niddah 31b:11:2.hebrew: שלא יהיו הכל שמחין - שאוכלין ושותין בסעודה, ואביו ואמו עצבים, שאסורין בתשמיש:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:11:2.english: So that not everyone will be happy - For they eat and drink at the feast, while his father and mother are sad, as they are forbidden from marital relations.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:12:1.english: A menstruating woman [for] seven [days] - [This] does not refer to a woman who has given birth.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:12:2.english: Because a man is accustomed to his wife - [At] any time that he desires.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:12:3.english: [He] is repulsed by her - [She becomes] repulsive to him. [Therefore] the Torah said: Whenever she sees [blood], she shall be [ritually] impure [for] seven [days], so that he will not be accustomed to her and she will become dear to him.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:13:1.english: Pursues a woman - An unmarried man seeks and pursues until he marries.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:14:2.hebrew: זהו ממקום שנברא - מסתכל באדמה שנוצר ממנה, והיא מסתכלת בו שנוצרה הימנו:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:14:2.english: This one [faces] the place from which he was created - [He] looks at the earth from which he was formed, and she looks at him from whom she was formed.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:15:1.english: Accepts appeasement - [He is] easy to appease.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:15:2.hebrew: זה ממקום שנברא - אדמה. עפר תיחוח נוח ליבטל, אבל בשר ועצמות קשין:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:15:2.english: This [man is] from the place from which he was created - [from] the earth. Loose earth is easily dissolved, whereas flesh and bones are hard.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:16:1.hebrew: עצם - כשמכין בו, קולו נשמע; אבל קרקע, כשמכין בו, אין קולו נשמע:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:16:1.english: A bone - When one strikes it, its sound is heard; but earth, when one strikes it, its sound is not heard.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:18:1.english: Samaritan girls are menstruants from their cradle - From their infancy. And in the Gemara, [it] explains the reason.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:18:2.english: Lower [bedding] like [the] upper [bedding] - [It] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:19:1.hebrew: והן יושבות על כל דם ודם - כלומר, להכי הוו בועלי נדות, משום דכל דם שרואות — בין אדום בין ירוק — יושבות עליו ימי נדות. וזו תקלה היא להם, שאם רואה דם ירוק היום, מתחלת למנות ששה והוא; אם תראה באותם ימי נדות דם אדום, אינה מונה אלא מיום ראייה ראשונה, ואותו דם ירוק טהור היה, ומראייה שניה היא צריכה למנות:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:19:1.english: And they sit [in observance of menstrual impurity] for each and every [type of] blood - That is to say, this is why they are [considered] men who engage in intercourse with menstruating women: because for any blood that they see — whether red or green — they observe the days of menstruation for it. And this is a stumbling block for them: for if she sees green blood today, she begins to count six [days] and it [the day of sighting]; if she [then] sees red blood during those days of menstruation, she counts only from the day of the first sighting, whereas that green blood was pure, and she needs to count from the second sighting.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:1:1.english: Who delay themselves - from emitting seed.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:1:2.english: I could - In that he delays himself from emitting seed.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:1:3.hebrew: יבעול וישנה - שמתוך תאות בעילה ראשונה תהא מזרעת, ונהי נמי דתזריע אחריו, תקדום הזרעתה בבעילה שניה:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:1:3.english: He should engage in intercourse and repeat - For out of the desire of the first intercourse, she will emit seed, and even though she may emit seed after him, her emission of seed will precede [his] in the second intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:20:1.hebrew: אין חייבין עליה - הלובש או מתכסה באותן בגדים ונכנס למקדש, פטור מקרבן; או אם נגעו אותן בגדים של משכב בתרומה, תולין, דלא ידעינן אי נדה היא אי לא. והא דאמר דמסתמא טמאות, גזירה דרבנן היא:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:20:1.english: One is not liable on its account - One who wears or covers himself with those garments and enters the Temple is exempt from [bringing] an offering; or if those garments used for lying touched terumah, one leaves [it] in suspense, for we do not know whether she is a niddah or not. And that which [the Mishnah] said that they are presumptively impure is a rabbinic decree.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:21:1.hebrew: אפילו דידן נמי - אי חזיא בעריסתן, טמאה, דתניא לקמן (נדה דף לב.): בת יום אחד לנדה מנין? תלמוד לומר "ואשה":
Rashi on Niddah 31b:21:1.english: Even our own also - If she sees [blood while] in their cradle, she is impure, as it is taught in a baraita later (Niddah 32a): From where [is it derived that] a one-day-old [girl is susceptible] to niddah [impurity]? The verse states: "And a woman."

Rashi on Niddah 31b:22:1.english: Since there is a minority who see [blood] - In their childhood.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:22:2.english: We are concerned for the minority - And we render all of them impure from their cradle, because perhaps she saw [menstrual blood].

Rashi on Niddah 31b:2:1.hebrew: בעון - על ידי דם נדה, שהוא סימן להריון, כדקיימא לן (כתובות דף י:): כל אשה שדמיה מרובין, בניה מרובין. והוא מביאו לידי עון, וקדייק ר' יצחק: "בעון" — שסמוך לעון נדות, שהוא מוזהר לפרוש הימנה:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:2:1.english: In iniquity - Through menstrual blood, which is a sign of [capacity for] pregnancy, as we hold (Ketubot 10b): "Any woman whose [menstrual] blood is abundant, her children are abundant." And it brings one to iniquity; and Rabbi Yitzchak infers [from] "in iniquity" [that conception occurs] close to the iniquity of menstruation, when he is warned to separate from her.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:3:1.hebrew: ובחטא - לשון טבילה וטהרה, כדמפרש. וה"ק: על ידי דם נדות, שהוא מביא לידי עון, חוללתי — שהוא גרם לי שנבראתי — וכשנתחטאת אמי ממנו, יחמתני:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:3:1.english: And in sin [uvḥet] - An expression of immersion and purification, as is explained [below]. And this is what [the verse] is saying: Through the blood of menstruation, which brings [one] to iniquity, "I was brought forth" — for it caused me to be created — and when my mother was purified from it, "she conceived me."

Rashi on Niddah 31b:5:1.english: Kar - A gift, which is a sign of peace.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:7:1.hebrew: נקיה - חסרה, כמו (ב"ק דף מא.) יצא פלוני נקי מנכסיו:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:7:1.english: Clean [nekiya] - Lacking, as [in] (Bava Kamma 41a): "So-and-so went out clean of his property."

Rashi on Niddah 31b:7:2.english: Until she says "sustenance" - [That is,] she knows how to pray.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:7:3.english: Specify [nokva] - When you specify and state your wages explicitly, [then] I will give it. And "female" [nekevah] is also expounded thus.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:8:1.english: Therefore, she must bring an offering - [The offering for] an oath of utterance, [which is] a sin-offering.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:9:1.hebrew: מזידה היא - ואין כאן קרבן, דהא "ונעלם" כתיב בשבועת ביטוי:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:9:1.english: She is an intentional violator - And there is no offering here, for "and it was concealed" is written regarding an oath of utterance.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:9:2.hebrew: ובחרטה תליא - לפתוח לה בחרטה ויתיר לה חכם שבועתה, אבל קרבן אינו עוקר ומתיר שבועתה:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:9:2.english: And on regret [it] depends - To open [a basis for annulment] for her with regret, and a sage will annul her oath; whereas an offering does not uproot and annul her oath.

Rashi on Niddah 31b:9:3.hebrew: ועוד קרבן שבועה בעי אתויי - כשבה או שעירה, והאי עוף הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 31b:9:3.english: And furthermore, she must bring an oath-offering - [Namely,] a female lamb or a female goat, whereas this [offering] is a bird.

Tosafot on Niddah 31b:16:1.english: "For sweet is your voice" - However, she does not praise him for [having] a sweet voice, but rather as "white and ruddy" [Song of Songs 5:10].

Tosafot on Niddah 31b:18:1.hebrew: בנות כותים - והן יושבות על כל דם ודם. ואם תאמר: ותיפוק ליה שהן נדות מעריסתן? ויש לומר: דהיינו דוקא בקטנותן, דלא דרשי "ואשה", כדאמר בגמרא; אבל גדולות, דמפרשי להו וטבלי, לא מטמו אלא משום דיושבות על כל דם ודם:
Tosafot on Niddah 31b:18:1.english: Samaritan girls - "And they observe [the seven-day period] for each and every [emission of] blood." And if you will say: Let [their impurity] be derived from the fact that they are menstruating women from their cradle! And one can say: That [applies] specifically in their childhood, when [the Samaritans] do not expound [the word] "and a woman" [ve'ishah], as is stated in the Gemara; but [as for] adult women, whom they separate [during menstruation] and who immerse, [the Samaritan men] only become impure because [the women] observe [the seven-day period] for each and every [emission of] blood:

Tosafot on Niddah 31b:18:2.hebrew: תחתון כעליון - מפרש בגמרא: תחתונו של בועל נדה כעליונו של זב, דלא מטמא אלא אוכלין ומשקין. ועליונו של זב, מפרש רשב"ם שהכריע הזב בכף מאזנים את האוכלין ומשקין שבכף שניה. ולא נהירא, דבפ' ר"ע (שבת דף פג.) קרי ליה היסט מה שהכריע הזב בכף מאזנים; והיסט נפקא לן מ"אשר יגע בהם הזב", ועליונו של זב נפקא לן בשמעתין מקרא אחרינא. ונראה דעליונו של זב היינו בגד שמקצתו על הזב ומקצתו נגרר על הארץ, ולאו היינו היסט, אלא כשמסיטו כולו, כדאמר: "איזהו מגעו שהוא ככולו? הוי אומר זה היסטו":
Tosafot on Niddah 31b:18:2.english: Lower [bedding] like the upper [bedding] - The Gemara explains: The lower [bedding] of one who engages in intercourse with a menstruating woman is like the upper [bedding] of a zav, which imparts impurity only to food and drink. And [regarding] the upper [bedding] of a zav, Rashbam explains that [it refers to a case where] the zav weighed down in a pan of a balance the food and drink that were in the second pan. But [this] does not seem [correct], for in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Akiva (Shabbat 83a), it calls [a case] where the zav weighed down [food and drink] in a pan of a balance "shifting" [heset]; and shifting is derived from [the verse], "whomsoever the zav touches," whereas the upper [bedding] of a zav is derived in our sugya from another verse. Rather, it appears that the upper [bedding] of a zav is a garment part of which is upon the zav and part of which drags on the ground; and it is not [considered] shifting unless he shifts all of it, as [the Gemara] says: "What is a touching of him that is like all of him? You must say, this is his shifting."
